title: Indian Racing Festival Brings FIA Racing Back To Buddh Circuit After 13 Years
excerpt: F4 Round 4 and Indian Racing League Round 2 run at Greater Noida on October 31 and November 1, with Luviwe Sambudla leading the F4 standings on 138 points.
body:
• The Indian Racing Festival brings the F4 Indian Championship and Indian Racing League to Buddh International Circuit in Greater Noida for the first time on October 31 and November 1.
  • The weekend is F4 Round 4 and IRL Round 2 of 2026, and marks the return of FIA-level racing to the circuit after 13 years.
  • Goa Aces JA Racing's Luviwe Sambudla leads F4 on 138 points, 21 ahead of Aris Kyriakou, after winning two races in Chennai.
  • BIC will host a second Festival weekend on November 28-29, before the season ends at the Navi Mumbai Street Circuit on December 5-6.

The Indian Racing Festival will bring the F4 Indian Championship and the Indian Racing League to the Buddh International Circuit in Greater Noida for the first time this weekend, with racing scheduled on October 31 and November 1 at the former Formula 1 venue.

The weekend is Round 4 of the F4 championship and Round 2 of the Indian Racing League for 2026. The circuit previously hosted the Formula 1 Indian Grand Prix and MotoGP Bharat, and spans 5.125 kilometres, according to a Festival press release reported by ANI via Devdiscourse. For fans in Delhi-NCR, it is a chance to watch the Festival at a permanent international-standard circuit closer to home.

Why the Buddh debut matters

Buddh International Circuit hosted the F1 Indian GP from 2011 to 2013. Because F4 India is an FIA-certified championship, its arrival marks the first time FIA-level racing has returned to the track after 13 years, Autocar India reported. The Festival will return to the same circuit for a second weekend on November 28-29, for F4 Round 5 and IRL Round 3, before the season closes elsewhere.

"The circuit previously hosted the Formula 1 Indian Grand Prix and MotoGP Bharat, and spans 5.125 kilometres, according to a Festival press release reported by ANI via Devdiscourse ."

The 2026 F4 season began in September with two rounds at Coimbatore's Kari Motor Speedway. The series then moved to Chennai's Madras International Circuit for Round 3 on October 22-23, which also hosted Round 1 of the 2026 Indian Racing League. The Festival will not race at the Goa Street Circuit this season, Autocar India reported.

Sambudla leads after Chennai

The F4 title fight arrives at Buddh with a new leader. Goa Aces JA Racing's Luviwe Sambudla started from sixth on the grid in Chennai, won each of the first two races and finished third in the final race, taking him to 138 points and a 21-point lead over Kichcha's Kings Bengaluru's Aris Kyriakou. Earlier in the season Kyriakou had led the championship, with Sambudla close behind.

Speed Demons Delhi's Ntiyiso Mabunda finished second in all three Chennai races, including a drive from 10th on the grid to second in the opening race. Kolkata Royal Tigers' Aaron Mehta won the third race from pole position, holding off Mabunda by 0.546 seconds, and at 15 years, six months and six days became the youngest winner in Indian F4 history, the press release said.

What happens after Buddh

The Indian Racing League heads into its second round at Buddh, with teams looking to strengthen their positions in the standings after the Chennai opener. No ticket details were stated in the sources read for this report, so readers should check the Festival and circuit channels for the latest entry information before travelling.

After the October 31-November 1 weekend, both championships return to Buddh on November 28-29. The season then ends at the Navi Mumbai Street Circuit on December 5-6. That 3.69-kilometre street circuit runs along Palm Beach Road, has an anti-clockwise layout with 11 turns, and will host the Festival's second night race, following the Chennai event in 2024. All rounds will be streamed live on JioHotstar and Star Sports in India, Autocar India reported.
